title: Public WebAssembly gamma and Riemann xi batches
objective: Route public complex gamma and Riemann xi heavy batches through the receipt-backed Arb/Acb WebAssembly analytic reactor with native oracle, enclosure tolerance, Node-Wasm/browser route, lifecycle, and benchmark crossing evidence
references: SageMath numerical gamma and Riemann xi semantics

oracles: Independent mpmath values and exact special values
Node-Wasm and Chromium execution of the production reactor

handoff.summary: Added explicitly numerical public complex_gamma/complex_gamma_values and riemann_xi/riemann_xi_values entry points. Heavy public batches make one receipt-backed Acb reactor call per family and preserve ComplexField precision; the xi API uses Sage.js's existing no-half normalization. The real packed reactor passes exact-value, >=150-bit enclosure, functional-equation, and release checks. Identical public source passes in Node-Wasm and Chromium with private analytic route counts of 2 rather than 256 for the matched scalar control. The recorded 128-point-per-family check reduces analytic crossings 128-fold and runs 1.77x faster.
risks: The public functions are intentionally numerical and do not claim Sage's complete symbolic gamma simplification surface.
Native Windows continues to use the documented tested-capability fallback until the shared Arb/Acb reactor is distributed there; missing complex-gamma capability raises explicitly.

Repository-wide integration was not repeated after the coordinator merged unrelated numeric/algebraic lanes; the coordinator confirmed no repeat long build was required because this lane's implementation and shared trace commits were already integrated.
next_steps: Integrate the final evidence-only normalization and crossing-accounting follow-up after the numeric-resource route instrumentation.
Retain shared capability, workload, and public-corpus registration in the coordinator lane.
